title: Microsoft Edge: organise and merge PDF files in the built-in PDF reader
summary: Hold: the controls table identifies the policy's scope as User without supporting documentation, while the prose correctly says its scope is not yet documented. The roadmap facts match the record, and independent searches confirmed the remaining documentation gaps.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to add PDF organising and merging to the built-in Microsoft Edge PDF reader.
claims.quote: Users can organize and merge PDF files in the Microsoft Edge built-in PDF reader.

claims.quote: They can select pages to extract, delete, rotate, or reorder, and save the result as a new PDF file.

claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge PDF organize merge license pricing subscription; Microsoft Edge for Business licensing prerequisites free browser license requirements. Read Edge PDF prerequisites and results on Edge for Business, Acrobat subscriptions and SharePoint merging; none licenses this feature.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the planned organising and merging feature, whose description here rests on the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge organize merge default; PdfOrganizeAndMergeEnabled Microsoft Edge PDF organize merge policy default per profile registry. Read microsoft-edge-pdf, searched the complete Edge policy list and Stable release notes; no description of this planned feature found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether this feature is enabled by default.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge organize merge default; PdfOrganizeAndMergeEnabled Microsoft Edge PDF organize merge policy default per profile registry. Read the roadmap and PDF reader page, searched Edge policies and Stable release notes; none states this feature's default.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and .api; summary; controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Neither an admin UI path nor an automation call for PdfOrganizeAndMergeEnabled is documented in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: PdfOrganizeAndMergeEnabled Microsoft Edge PDF organize merge policy default per profile registry. Searched the complete Edge policy list, including PDF Reader; no entry. Opened /deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies/pdforganizeandmergeenabled; web fetch confirmed HTTP 404.

claims.claim: The PdfOrganizeAndMergeEnabled control has user scope.
claims.quote: Searched: PdfOrganizeAndMergeEnabled Microsoft Edge PDF organize merge policy default per profile registry; complete Edge policy list and its expected reference URL. No scope found. The briefing itself says 'its scope (device or user) ... [is] not yet documented'.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].scope to 'other' and replace the rendered table's 'User' scope label with 'Other'. Keep the existing prose stating that device or user scope is not yet documented; do not identify the policy as user-scoped without documentation.

claims.claim: Whether merged or extracted output preserves protection from source PDFs is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge merge PDF protection; Microsoft Edge organize merge PDF licensing price protected files protection operating systems version. Read PDF reader Protected PDFs and returned protection excerpts; no preservation rule for this planned merging/extraction feature found.

claims.claim: The roadmap and PDF reader page do not describe how organising or merging treats protected PDFs.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge merge PDF protection. Read full roadmap and microsoft-edge-pdf, including Protected PDFs, and returned protection excerpts; these describe general viewing and permissions, not organising or merging protected PDFs.

claims.claim: The Edge PDF reader documentation describes opening MIP-protected PDF files.
claims.quote: With Microsoft Edge, users can view MIP protected files saved locally, or in the cloud.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes user-selected page and file operations, not autonomous actions.
claims.quote: They can select pages to extract, delete, rotate, or reorder, and save the result as a new PDF file. They can also merge the open PDF file with other PDF files

claims.claim: Learn documents configuring Edge policy settings with group policy objects.
claims.quote: You can use group policy objects (GPO) to configure policy settings for Microsoft Edge and managed Microsoft Edge updates on all versions of Windows.

claims.claim: Learn documents configuring Edge policies through the registry.
claims.quote: You can also configure policies via the registry for: Windows devices that are joined to a Microsoft Active Directory (AD) domain; Windows 10 Pro or Enterprise instances enrolled for device management in Microsoft Intune

claims.claim: The Edge policy reference links to individual policy pages for details.
claims.quote: These tables list all of the browser-related group policies available in this release of Microsoft Edge. Use the links in the table to get more details about specific policies.

claims.claim: Opening edge://policy in Edge on a target device shows the applied policies.
claims.quote: On a target client device, open Microsoft Edge and go to edge://policy to see all policies that are applied.
